title: Count the distinct clients

prereqs.why: The answer is a pipeline, and which tool goes where is the whole question.

statement:
An access log, `access.log`, in the usual combined format. The client IP is the **first whitespace-separated field** of each line:

```
203.0.113.8 - - [03/Oct/2026:14:22:01 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 5120
198.51.100.2 - - [03/Oct/2026:14:22:03 +0000] "GET /style.css HTTP/1.1" 200 1024
203.0.113.8 - - [03/Oct/2026:14:22:04 +0000] "POST /api/v1 HTTP/1.1" 201 64
```

The file has forty million lines.

**Write a one-line pipeline that prints just the number of distinct client IPs.** Nothing else — one number on stdout.

Any of the obvious tools is fine; several spellings are accepted.
hints: You need three things: pull out the first field, reduce it to distinct values, and count the lines that come out.
`uniq` only removes *adjacent* duplicates, so something has to happen before it. Or skip it — `sort` has a flag that does both.
`wc -l` counts lines. `cut -f1 -d' '` and `awk '{print $1}'` both pull a field.
